caseVerdicts.scientificReason: The stipulated pure KBr/KCl binary set, matching references and a negative reagent blank support KBr from the cream/pale-yellow AgBr observation. Ag+ + Br− -> AgBr has balanced Ag/Br and total charge zero on both sides. Dilute HNO3 pretreatment is appropriate to suppress carbonate interference without introducing the target halide. HCl itself supplies chloride and can produce AgCl in an originally chloride-free sample; this is correctly separated from original-sample chloride evidence. Counterion K+ comes from the binary premise, not the silver test. The mixture transfer properly withholds exclusive bromide, pure salt and mass-fraction claims. The bound is chemically adequate without requiring ammonia differentiation as a universal new task quota.
caseVerdicts.interferenceAndSafetyBoundary: Cream-white mixed precipitates cannot support unrestricted unique identification. Supplied controlled observations are a written case, with no invitation to perform a silver/nitric-acid test. The RSC source establishes dilute reagents, eye protection, contamination control and appropriate professional handling; this method reference is not a German curricular source.
caseVerdicts.operativeScopeReason: Current a44 selected-ion goal is applicable and target-visible in all four actual BB/BE GK/LK views. The old substitution-specific 413 goal is read for supplementary test/control knowledge and is not promoted to an absent operative target.

caseVerdicts.scientificReason: The explicit pure Na2CO3/NaCl premise excludes hydrogencarbonate, sulfite and other gas-forming constituents. Controlled acid treatment followed by a separate CO2/limewater response identifies the carbonate candidate in this limited set. CO3^2− + 2 H3O+ -> CO2 + 3 H2O conserves C1/O5/H6 and total charge zero. CO2 + Ca(OH)2 -> CaCO3 + H2O explains precipitation. Na+ remains a spectator; neither gas bubbles nor the qualitative limewater response gives an amount. Fresh inclusion of NaHCO3 correctly leaves carbonate/hydrogencarbonate unresolved because HCO3− + H3O+ -> CO2 + 2 H2O gives the same gas. The supplied excess-CO2 dissolution CaCO3 + CO2 + H2O -> Ca2+ + 2 HCO3− conserves C2/O6/H2 and charge zero; a clear endpoint cannot erase the recorded initial positive gas response.
caseVerdicts.interferenceAndSafetyBoundary: The response is not a universal starting-ion test. Separate teacher-controlled model portions, blank/positive controls, fresh limewater and the excluded alternative gases are necessary. No unsupervised acid/gas handling or actual learner performance is asserted.
caseVerdicts.operativeScopeReason: The carbonate witness is hosted by the currently visible a44 selected-ion goal. Existing 580 CO2 cases are retained only as gas-evidence support, because a CO2 test alone does not identify original carbonate. No additional O2/H2 whole-family duty is introduced.

caseVerdicts.scientificReason: Under the stated aqueous NH4Cl/NaCl binary set, a controlled gas response after hydroxide treatment and warming supports NH4+ when reagent and NaCl blanks are negative, an ammonium control is positive, and contact/alkaline-droplet transfer are excluded. NH4+ + OH− -> NH3 + H2O conserves N1/O1/H5 and charge zero. NH4+ donates a proton and OH− accepts it. Neutral gaseous NH3 is distinct from the original aqueous ammonium ion. In damp indicator paper NH3 + H2O <-> NH4+ + OH− explains the basic response. Direct NaOH contact also turns paper blue, so it is not ammonium evidence. Pre-existing ammonia or other volatile basic species correctly defeat the unrestricted transfer inference. The chloride counterion is known only from the candidate set; no quantitative or general gas-specific identification is claimed.
caseVerdicts.interferenceAndSafetyBoundary: The task uses supplied fictional observations, controlled warming and separated damp indicator paper. This matches the RSC carefully warmed, non-spitting hydroxide method without inviting direct smelling or an unsupervised laboratory procedure. Exclusion of alkaline droplets is material to the inference, not an optional stylistic condition.
